tool_args.content:
Full-width academic concept figure for EMNLP 2026 (16x6 inches, 300 DPI, pure white background). This is the hero figure illustrating "Recursive Generation Depth Estimation."

LAYOUT: Three vertically stacked panels with generous spacing.

==== PANEL (a) — TOP 38%: RECURSIVE GENERATION CHAIN ====

Title "(a) Recursive Generation Chain" in 12pt bold serif #3B4A5C, left-aligned above the panel.

Large rounded container (background #F7F8FA, border #E8ECF0 0.5pt, corner-radius 12px).

Four rounded boxes connected by arrows, left to right:

BOX D0: fill #D6EAF8, border #85B2D3.
  Tiny document icon top-right. Center: italic "D0" in 16pt bold serif.
  Below: "Human" in 8pt #6B7B8D. Bottom: "seed corpus" in 6pt italic #8899B0.

BOX D1: fill #EAE0D4, border #C8B8A4.
  "D1", "Gen-1". Bottom: "1st-gen synthetic" in 6pt italic.

BOX D2: fill #E0CEB0, border #C0A888.
  "D2", "Gen-2". Bottom: "2nd-gen synthetic" in 6pt italic.

Three dots "..." between D2 and DK.

BOX DK: fill #C4A47A, border #A08050.
  "DK", "Gen-K" in lighter text #F0E8DC. Bottom: "K-th gen" in 6pt italic.

Between boxes: small "LLM θ" badge ABOVE arrow, "LoRA ft + sample" BELOW arrow.
Bottom of panel: thin gradient bar from blue-gray to warm tan, label "distribution shift accumulates →".

==== PANEL (b) — MIDDLE 42%: DEPTH ESTIMATION PIPELINE ====

Title "(b) Depth Estimation Pipeline" in 12pt bold serif #3B4A5C.

Dashed arrow from Panel (a) to text passage element.

FOUR main elements left to right:

1. Text Passage: Document icon with gray lines. Below: "Text passage x" in bold. Below: "depth d = ?" in italic red #C0392B.

2. Feature Extraction box: "19 Statistical Features" title. Inside: 2x2 grid of 4 colored blocks:
   - "Perplexity (9)" with "mean, var, skew, kurt, p10-p90"
   - "Surprisal (3)" with "mean, var, entropy"
   - "Lexical (4)" with "TTR, hapax, n-gram H"
   - "Repetition (3)" with "rep. 2/3/4-gram"

3. Classifier: Dark navy box (#2C3E50), "Random Forest" in WHITE, "200 trees" in #8BA0B4.

4. Prediction Output: Bar chart with 4 bars (d=0: 8%, d=1: 70%, d=2: 15%, d=K: 5%). Colors: #D6EAF8, #C4A47A, #D4B896, #A08050. "70%" and "15%" labels above bars. Below chart: "d-hat = 1" in bold.

INSET in upper-right of Panel (b): Mini line chart "Tail Decay Signal" showing declining p90 perplexity from d=0 to d=3, with circle markers on a warm-colored line.

==== PANEL (c) — BOTTOM 20%: TASK COMPARISON ====

CRITICAL: This panel shows a SIDE-BY-SIDE COMPARISON of two approaches, NOT a pipeline.

Title "(c) Task Comparison" in 12pt bold serif #3B4A5C.

LEFT box: "Binary Detection" — light gray background (#F5F6F8), muted text #AAAAAA, label "real vs. synthetic" in #BBBBBB. Small cross symbol in muted rose.

"vs." text between the two boxes.

RIGHT box (highlighted): Warm background (#F5F0EA), border #C4A47A.
  "Ours: ordinal depth estimation" in bold #5B4A30.
  "d-hat in {0, 1, ..., K}" in serif.
  "4-class RF: 78.4% acc (chance 25%)" in green #27AE60.
  Small checkmark in green.

==== STYLE ====
- Publication quality for EMNLP/NeurIPS
- Elegant, premium, sophisticated
- Subtle drop shadows on boxes
- Rounded corners everywhere
- Serif font (Times New Roman) for main text
- PALETTE: #D6EAF8 #85B2D3 #EAE0D4 #C8B8A4 #E0CEB0 #C0A888 #C4A47A #A08050 #D4B896 #2C3E50 #3B4A5C #8899B0 #F7F8FA #E8ECF0
- Cool-to-warm gradient from D0 to DK is the KEY visual metaphor
- NO matplotlib defaults, NO gray background, NO clipart

tool_args.content:
Full-width academic concept figure for EMNLP 2026 (16x6 inches, 300 DPI, pure white background). Illustrates "Recursive Generation Depth Estimation" — the complete visual summary of the paper.

LAYOUT: Three vertically stacked panels.

==== PANEL (a) — TOP 35%: RECURSIVE GENERATION CHAIN ====

Title "(a) Recursive Generation Chain" in bold serif #3B4A5C.

Large rounded container (light gray #F7F8FA background).

Four rounded boxes with EXTRA-WIDE spacing (enough for one-line labels):

BOX D0: cool blue-gray fill #D6EAF8. Document icon top-right. Center: "D0" bold. Below: "Human". Bottom line: "seed corpus" italic small.
BOX D1: warm beige fill #EAE0D4. "D1", "Gen-1", "1st-gen synthetic".
BOX D2: warmer fill #E0CEB0. "D2", "Gen-2", "2nd-gen synthetic".
Three dots "..." in gray.
BOX DK: deep tan fill #C4A47A. "DK", "Gen-K", "K-th gen" in light text.

Between each pair: rounded "LLM θ" badge ABOVE arrow. Below arrow ON ONE LINE: "LoRA ft + sample" (ensure wide enough spacing so this fits on one line without wrapping).

Bottom of panel: thin gradient bar from blue-gray to tan. Right-aligned label: "distribution shift accumulates →".

==== PANEL (b) — MIDDLE 42%: DEPTH ESTIMATION PIPELINE ====

Title "(b) Depth Estimation Pipeline" in bold serif.

Dashed arrow from Panel (a) down to text passage.

LEFT: Document icon. Below: "Text passage x" bold. Below: "depth d = ?" italic rust-red.

Arrow → FEATURE EXTRACTION box: Title "19 Statistical Features" bold. Inside 2x2 grid:
  Top-left: "Perplexity (9)" — "mean, var, skew, kurt, p10-p90" in tiny text
  Top-right: "Surprisal (3)" — "mean, var, entropy"
  Bottom-left: "Lexical (4)" — "TTR, hapax, n-gram H"
  Bottom-right: "Repetition (3)" — "rep. 2/3/4-gram"

Arrow → CLASSIFIER box: Dark navy #2C3E50 background. "Random Forest" in WHITE bold. "200 trees" in light blue-gray.

Arrow → PREDICTION box: Light background. Mini bar chart with exactly 4 bars:
  d=0: tiny bar (8%), color #D6EAF8
  d=1: tallest bar (70%), color #C4A47A, "70%" above
  d=2: medium bar (15%), color #D4B896, "15%" above
  d=K: tiny bar (5%), color #A08050
  Labels below: d=0, d=1, d=2, d=K
  Below chart: "d-hat = 1" in bold.

INSET (upper-right area of Panel b): Small line chart titled "Tail Decay Signal". Shows a DECLINING LINE from d=0 to d=3 with 4 circle markers. Y-axis: "p90 ppl". The line descends from upper-left to lower-right, showing perplexity decreases with depth. Warm-colored line #C4A47A. Label: "primary depth signal" in tiny italic.

==== PANEL (c) — BOTTOM 18%: TASK COMPARISON ====

Title "(c) Task Comparison" in bold serif.

SIDE-BY-SIDE comparison (NOT a pipeline):

LEFT box (de-emphasized): Gray background #F5F6F8. "Binary Detection" in muted gray #AAAAAA. "real vs. synthetic" in lighter gray. Red cross mark.

Center: "vs." in light gray.

RIGHT box (highlighted): Warm background #F5F0EA, golden border #C4A47A. "Ours: ordinal depth estimation" in bold dark brown #5B4A30. "d-hat in {0, 1, ..., K}" in serif. Below: "4-class RF: 78.4% acc (chance 25%)" in green #27AE60. Green checkmark.

==== STYLE ====
Publication quality. Elegant serif typography. Muted academic palette. Subtle shadows. Rounded corners. NO matplotlib defaults, NO clipart. Cool-to-warm gradient from D0 to DK.

1	\section{Related Work}
2	\label{sec:related}

4	\paragraph{Model Collapse Theory.}
5	Recursive training on model outputs erodes distributional tails \cite{shumailov2024_nature}, an effect formalized as exponential tail decay via scaling laws \cite{dohmatob2024_tale_of_tails,seddik2024synthetic} and extended to autophagous loops in the MAD framework \cite{alemohammad2024_mad} and Markovian generation chains \cite{geng2026_markovian}.
6	Subsequent work refines the conditions under which collapse occurs: \citet{bertrand2024_stability} identify convergence to a fixed point under mixed real-synthetic retraining (providing theoretical grounding for our EDD ceiling, \S\ref{sec:method:theory}), \citet{shi2025_closer_look} reframe collapse as a generalization-to-memorization transition, and \citet{dohmatob2025_strong_collapse} extend guarantees to broader model classes.
7	\citet{schaeffer2025} argue that ``model collapse'' conflates multiple phenomena; we respond by operationalizing tail-erosion into a deployable ordinal classifier that reveals strategy-dependent trajectories the theory does not predict.
8	All assume depth is known a priori; we address the inverse problem of estimating depth from text alone.
9	
10	\paragraph{AI Text Detection.}
11	The detection literature \cite{wu2025_detection_survey} spans statistical \cite{mitchell2023_detectgpt,fast_detectgpt2024,binoculars2024,diveye2026,guo2024_biscope,gehrmann2019_gltr,verma2024_ghostbuster,yang2024_dnagpt}, geometric \cite{tulchinskii2023_intrinsic_dim}, and watermarking \cite{kirchenbauer2023_watermark} methods, with known limits \cite{sadasivan2023_paraphrase,pudasaini2026_detection_fails,pu2026_generator_barrier}.
12	\citet{bevendorff2025_two_paradigms} distinguish attribution from verification; depth estimation introduces a third axis: recursive iteration.
13	All perform binary classification; our approach outputs ordinal depth labels, complementing rather than replacing detection.
14
